title: 1 Kings 8: The Ark Brought In and the Temple Dedicated
body:
Read the chapter → [1 Kings 8](/bible/1-kings/8)

**[1 Kings 8:1-5](/bible/1-kings/8#v1)**
> <sup>[1](/bible/1-kings/8#v1)</sup> Then Solomon assembled the elders of Israel, and all the heads of the tribes, the chief of the fathers of the children of Israel, unto king Solomon in Jerusalem, that they might bring up the ark of the covenant of the Lord out of the city of David, which is Zion.
>
> <sup>[2](/bible/1-kings/8#v2)</sup> And all the men of Israel assembled themselves unto king Solomon at the feast in the month Ethanim, which is the seventh month.
>
> <sup>[3](/bible/1-kings/8#v3)</sup> And all the elders of Israel came, and the priests took up the ark.
>
> <sup>[4](/bible/1-kings/8#v4)</sup> And they brought up the ark of the Lord, and the tabernacle of the congregation, and all the holy vessels that were in the tabernacle, even those did the priests and the Levites bring up.
>
> <sup>[5](/bible/1-kings/8#v5)</sup> And king Solomon, and all the congregation of Israel, that were assembled unto him, were with him before the ark, sacrificing sheep and oxen, that could not be told nor numbered for multitude.

- Solomon assembles the elders of Israel and the heads of the tribes to bring up the ark of the covenant out of the city of David, which is Zion, in the month Ethanim, the seventh month, at the feast. This gathering is a feast of dedication for the temple, not the later feast of dedication remembered in Maccabees, but a first feasting to dedicate the house of the Lord.
- The priests and Levites bring up the ark, the tabernacle of the congregation, and all the holy vessels, while Solomon and all the congregation sacrifice sheep and oxen that could not be numbered for multitude.

**[1 Kings 8:6-9](/bible/1-kings/8#v6)**
> <sup>[6](/bible/1-kings/8#v6)</sup> And the priests brought in the ark of the covenant of the Lord unto his place, into the oracle of the house, to the most holy place, even under the wings of the cherubims.
>
> <sup>[7](/bible/1-kings/8#v7)</sup> For the cherubims spread forth their two wings over the place of the ark, and the cherubims covered the ark and the staves thereof above.
>
> <sup>[8](/bible/1-kings/8#v8)</sup> And they drew out the staves, that the ends of the staves were seen out in the holy place before the oracle, and they were not seen without: and there they are unto this day.
>
> <sup>[9](/bible/1-kings/8#v9)</sup> There was nothing in the ark save the two tables of stone, which Moses put there at Horeb, when the Lord made a covenant with the children of Israel, when they came out of the land of Egypt.

- The priests bring the ark into the oracle, the most holy place, under the wings of the cherubims, whose wings spread over the place of the ark and covered it and the staves. The staves, the handles for carrying the ark, are drawn out so their ends are seen in the holy place before the oracle but not seen without, and there they remain.
- There is nothing in the ark save the two tables of stone that Moses put there at Horeb, when the Lord made the covenant with Israel as they came out of Egypt.

**[1 Kings 8:10-13](/bible/1-kings/8#v10)**
> <sup>[10](/bible/1-kings/8#v10)</sup> And it came to pass, when the priests were come out of the holy place, that the cloud filled the house of the Lord,
>
> <sup>[11](/bible/1-kings/8#v11)</sup> So that the priests could not stand to minister because of the cloud: for the glory of the Lord had filled the house of the Lord.
>
> <sup>[12](/bible/1-kings/8#v12)</sup> Then spake Solomon, The Lord said that he would dwell in the thick darkness.
>
> <sup>[13](/bible/1-kings/8#v13)</sup> I have surely built thee an house to dwell in, a settled place for thee to abide in for ever.

- When the priests come out of the holy place, the cloud fills the house of the Lord so that they cannot stand to minister, for the glory of the Lord filled the house. Solomon says the Lord said he would dwell in the thick darkness, and that he has built a house for the Most High to abide in forever.

**[1 Kings 8:14-21](/bible/1-kings/8#v14)**
> <sup>[14](/bible/1-kings/8#v14)</sup> And the king turned his face about, and blessed all the congregation of Israel: (and all the congregation of Israel stood;)
>
> <sup>[15](/bible/1-kings/8#v15)</sup> And he said, Blessed be the Lord God of Israel, which spake with his mouth unto David my father, and hath with his hand fulfilled it, saying,
>
> <sup>[16](/bible/1-kings/8#v16)</sup> Since the day that I brought forth my people Israel out of Egypt, I chose no city out of all the tribes of Israel to build an house, that my name might be therein; but I chose David to be over my people Israel.
>
> <sup>[17](/bible/1-kings/8#v17)</sup> And it was in the heart of David my father to build an house for the name of the Lord God of Israel.
>
> <sup>[18](/bible/1-kings/8#v18)</sup> And the Lord said unto David my father, Whereas it was in thine heart to build an house unto my name, thou didst well that it was in thine heart.
>
> <sup>[19](/bible/1-kings/8#v19)</sup> Nevertheless thou shalt not build the house; but thy son that shall come forth out of thy loins, he shall build the house unto my name.
>
> <sup>[20](/bible/1-kings/8#v20)</sup> And the Lord hath performed his word that he spake, and I am risen up in the room of David my father, and sit on the throne of Israel, as the Lord promised, and have built an house for the name of the Lord God of Israel.
>
> <sup>[21](/bible/1-kings/8#v21)</sup> And I have set there a place for the ark, wherein is the covenant of the Lord, which he made with our fathers, when he brought them out of the land of Egypt.

- Solomon turns his face about and blesses all the congregation of Israel, standing before them, a black king addressing the whole nation of his people. He blesses the Lord God of Israel who spoke with his mouth to David and fulfilled it with his hand.
- He recounts that since the day the Most High brought Israel out of Egypt he chose no city to build a house, but chose David, and though it was in David's heart to build the house, the Lord said his son would build it. That word is now fulfilled, Solomon risen up in David's room, sitting on the throne, having built the house and set a place for the ark of the covenant.

**[1 Kings 8:22-30](/bible/1-kings/8#v22)**
> <sup>[22](/bible/1-kings/8#v22)</sup> And Solomon stood before the altar of the Lord in the presence of all the congregation of Israel, and spread forth his hands toward heaven:
>
> <sup>[23](/bible/1-kings/8#v23)</sup> And he said, Lord God of Israel, there is no God like thee, in heaven above, or on earth beneath, who keepest covenant and mercy with thy servants that walk before thee with all their heart:
>
> <sup>[24](/bible/1-kings/8#v24)</sup> Who hast kept with thy servant David my father that thou promisedst him: thou spakest also with thy mouth, and hast fulfilled it with thine hand, as it is this day.
>
> <sup>[25](/bible/1-kings/8#v25)</sup> Therefore now, Lord God of Israel, keep with thy servant David my father that thou promisedst him, saying, There shall not fail thee a man in my sight to sit on the throne of Israel; so that thy children take heed to their way, that they walk before me as thou hast walked before me.
>
> <sup>[26](/bible/1-kings/8#v26)</sup> And now, O God of Israel, let thy word, I pray thee, be verified, which thou spakest unto thy servant David my father.
>
> <sup>[27](/bible/1-kings/8#v27)</sup> But will God indeed dwell on the earth? behold, the heaven and heaven of heavens cannot contain thee; how much less this house that I have builded?
>
> <sup>[28](/bible/1-kings/8#v28)</sup> Yet have thou respect unto the prayer of thy servant, and to his supplication, O Lord my God, to hearken unto the cry and to the prayer, which thy servant prayeth before thee to day:
>
> <sup>[29](/bible/1-kings/8#v29)</sup> That thine eyes may be open toward this house night and day, even toward the place of which thou hast said, My name shall be there: that thou mayest hearken unto the prayer which thy servant shall make toward this place.
>
> <sup>[30](/bible/1-kings/8#v30)</sup> And hearken thou to the supplication of thy servant, and of thy people Israel, when they shall pray toward this place: and hear thou in heaven thy dwelling place: and when thou hearest, forgive.

- Solomon stands before the altar in the presence of all the congregation and spreads forth his hands toward heaven, praying that there is no God like the Lord in heaven above or earth beneath, who keeps covenant and mercy with those who walk before him. He asks the Most High to keep the promise to David that his seed shall not fail a man on the throne, if his children take heed to walk before him.
- Solomon confesses that the heaven of heavens cannot contain the Most High, how much less this house, yet he asks that the Lord's eyes be open toward this house night and day, and that he hearken to the prayers made toward this place and forgive. This teaches us to face our homeland and pray, and to build a prayer life like our forefathers.

**[1 Kings 8:31-40](/bible/1-kings/8#v31)**
> <sup>[31](/bible/1-kings/8#v31)</sup> If any man trespass against his neighbour, and an oath be laid upon him to cause him to swear, and the oath come before thine altar in this house:
>
> <sup>[32](/bible/1-kings/8#v32)</sup> Then hear thou in heaven, and do, and judge thy servants, condemning the wicked, to bring his way upon his head; and justifying the righteous, to give him according to his righteousness.
>
> <sup>[33](/bible/1-kings/8#v33)</sup> When thy people Israel be smitten down before the enemy, because they have sinned against thee, and shall turn again to thee, and confess thy name, and pray, and make supplication unto thee in this house:
>
> <sup>[34](/bible/1-kings/8#v34)</sup> Then hear thou in heaven, and forgive the sin of thy people Israel, and bring them again unto the land which thou gavest unto their fathers.
>
> <sup>[35](/bible/1-kings/8#v35)</sup> When heaven is shut up, and there is no rain, because they have sinned against thee; if they pray toward this place, and confess thy name, and turn from their sin, when thou afflictest them:
>
> <sup>[36](/bible/1-kings/8#v36)</sup> Then hear thou in heaven, and forgive the sin of thy servants, and of thy people Israel, that thou teach them the good way wherein they should walk, and give rain upon thy land, which thou hast given to thy people for an inheritance.
>
> <sup>[37](/bible/1-kings/8#v37)</sup> If there be in the land famine, if there be pestilence, blasting, mildew, locust, or if there be caterpiller; if their enemy besiege them in the land of their cities; whatsoever plague, whatsoever sickness there be;
>
> <sup>[38](/bible/1-kings/8#v38)</sup> What prayer and supplication soever be made by any man, or by all thy people Israel, which shall know every man the plague of his own heart, and spread forth his hands toward this house:
>
> <sup>[39](/bible/1-kings/8#v39)</sup> Then hear thou in heaven thy dwelling place, and forgive, and do, and give to every man according to his ways, whose heart thou knowest; (for thou, even thou only, knowest the hearts of all the children of men;)
>
> <sup>[40](/bible/1-kings/8#v40)</sup> That they may fear thee all the days that they live in the land which thou gavest unto our fathers.

- Solomon lays out the causes for which Israel would pray toward this house: when a man trespasses and swears before the altar, that the Lord judge between the wicked and the righteous; when Israel is smitten before the enemy for sin and turns again and confesses, that the Lord forgive and bring them back; when heaven is shut up and there is no rain because of sin, that he forgive and give rain.
- The weather itself, the rain and the drought, is bound to whether Israel is in sin or not, for the whole world and the sun, moon, and stars were made for the children of Israel. Solomon adds that when any plague of a man's own heart drives him to spread his hands toward this house, the Lord who alone knows the hearts of men will hear, forgive, and give to every man according to his ways.

**[1 Kings 8:41-45](/bible/1-kings/8#v41)**
> <sup>[41](/bible/1-kings/8#v41)</sup> Moreover concerning a stranger, that is not of thy people Israel, but cometh out of a far country for thy name’s sake;
>
> <sup>[42](/bible/1-kings/8#v42)</sup> (For they shall hear of thy great name, and of thy strong hand, and of thy stretched out arm;) when he shall come and pray toward this house;
>
> <sup>[43](/bible/1-kings/8#v43)</sup> Hear thou in heaven thy dwelling place, and do according to all that the stranger calleth to thee for: that all people of the earth may know thy name, to fear thee, as do thy people Israel; and that they may know that this house, which I have builded, is called by thy name.
>
> <sup>[44](/bible/1-kings/8#v44)</sup> If thy people go out to battle against their enemy, whithersoever thou shalt send them, and shall pray unto the Lord toward the city which thou hast chosen, and toward the house that I have built for thy name:
>
> <sup>[45](/bible/1-kings/8#v45)</sup> Then hear thou in heaven their prayer and their supplication, and maintain their cause.

- Solomon prays that even a stranger of a far country who hears of the great name and strong hand of the Most High and comes to pray toward this house be heard, that all people of the earth may know the name of the Lord and fear him as Israel does. This hearing of the nations comes only when Israel is right and in rulership, not while Israel is in captivity and sin.
- He prays that when Israel goes out to battle against the enemy in the way the Lord sends them and prays toward the city and the house, the Lord hear their prayer and maintain their cause. So the Most High hears the stranger's prayer out of respect for Israel, but he does not hear a prayer aimed against his people.
  - **[Zechariah 8:23](/bible/zechariah/8#v23)**
    > <sup>[23](/bible/zechariah/8#v23)</sup> Thus saith the Lord of hosts; In those days it shall come to pass, that ten men shall take hold out of all languages of the nations, even shall take hold of the skirt of him that is a Jew, saying, We will go with you: for we have heard that God is with you.

    In those days ten men out of all languages of the nations shall take hold of the skirt of him that is a Jew, saying, We will go with you, for we have heard that God is with you, the same joining of the nations to the house of Jacob that Solomon foresaw.

**[1 Kings 8:46-53](/bible/1-kings/8#v46)**
> <sup>[46](/bible/1-kings/8#v46)</sup> If they sin against thee, (for there is no man that sinneth not,) and thou be angry with them, and deliver them to the enemy, so that they carry them away captives unto the land of the enemy, far or near;
>
> <sup>[47](/bible/1-kings/8#v47)</sup> Yet if they shall bethink themselves in the land whither they were carried captives, and repent, and make supplication unto thee in the land of them that carried them captives, saying, We have sinned, and have done perversely, we have committed wickedness;
>
> <sup>[48](/bible/1-kings/8#v48)</sup> And so return unto thee with all their heart, and with all their soul, in the land of their enemies, which led them away captive, and pray unto thee toward their land, which thou gavest unto their fathers, the city which thou hast chosen, and the house which I have built for thy name:
>
> <sup>[49](/bible/1-kings/8#v49)</sup> Then hear thou their prayer and their supplication in heaven thy dwelling place, and maintain their cause,
>
> <sup>[50](/bible/1-kings/8#v50)</sup> And forgive thy people that have sinned against thee, and all their transgressions wherein they have transgressed against thee, and give them compassion before them who carried them captive, that they may have compassion on them:
>
> <sup>[51](/bible/1-kings/8#v51)</sup> For they be thy people, and thine inheritance, which thou broughtest forth out of Egypt, from the midst of the furnace of iron:
>
> <sup>[52](/bible/1-kings/8#v52)</sup> That thine eyes may be open unto the supplication of thy servant, and unto the supplication of thy people Israel, to hearken unto them in all that they call for unto thee.
>
> <sup>[53](/bible/1-kings/8#v53)</sup> For thou didst separate them from among all the people of the earth, to be thine inheritance, as thou spakest by the hand of Moses thy servant, when thou broughtest our fathers out of Egypt, O Lord God.

- Solomon prays for the day Israel sins and is carried captive to the land of the enemy, far or near, that if they bethink themselves, repent, and turn again with all their heart, confessing plainly the wickedness they have done, the Lord hear their prayer, maintain their cause, and forgive. He asks that the Most High give them compassion before those who carried them captive.
- No other nation on the earth has this way out, that when it sins it can always turn to the Most High, face the east, and pray for forgiveness, because he separated Israel from among all people of the earth to be his inheritance, brought forth out of the furnace of iron of Egypt. The luxuries Israel is afforded even in captivity are because the Lord is on their side.

**[1 Kings 8:54-61](/bible/1-kings/8#v54)**
> <sup>[54](/bible/1-kings/8#v54)</sup> And it was so, that when Solomon had made an end of praying all this prayer and supplication unto the Lord, he arose from before the altar of the Lord, from kneeling on his knees with his hands spread up to heaven.
>
> <sup>[55](/bible/1-kings/8#v55)</sup> And he stood, and blessed all the congregation of Israel with a loud voice, saying,
>
> <sup>[56](/bible/1-kings/8#v56)</sup> Blessed be the Lord, that hath given rest unto his people Israel, according to all that he promised: there hath not failed one word of all his good promise, which he promised by the hand of Moses his servant.
>
> <sup>[57](/bible/1-kings/8#v57)</sup> The Lord our God be with us, as he was with our fathers: let him not leave us, nor forsake us:
>
> <sup>[58](/bible/1-kings/8#v58)</sup> That he may incline our hearts unto him, to walk in all his ways, and to keep his commandments, and his statutes, and his judgments, which he commanded our fathers.
>
> <sup>[59](/bible/1-kings/8#v59)</sup> And let these my words, wherewith I have made supplication before the Lord, be nigh unto the Lord our God day and night, that he maintain the cause of his servant, and the cause of his people Israel at all times, as the matter shall require:
>
> <sup>[60](/bible/1-kings/8#v60)</sup> That all the people of the earth may know that the Lord is God, and that there is none else.
>
> <sup>[61](/bible/1-kings/8#v61)</sup> Let your heart therefore be perfect with the Lord our God, to walk in his statutes, and to keep his commandments, as at this day.

- When Solomon finishes praying he rises from kneeling with his hands spread to heaven and blesses all the congregation with a loud voice, blessing the Lord who has given rest to his people, not one word failing of all his good promise by the hand of Moses. He asks that the Lord be with them as with their fathers, incline their hearts to keep his commandments, statutes, and judgments.
- He asks that his words of supplication be near the Lord day and night, that the Most High maintain the cause of his people at all times, that all the people of the earth may know the Lord is God and there is none else. Therefore let the heart be perfect with the Lord, to walk in his statutes and keep his commandments.

**[1 Kings 8:62-66](/bible/1-kings/8#v62)**
> <sup>[62](/bible/1-kings/8#v62)</sup> And the king, and all Israel with him, offered sacrifice before the Lord.
>
> <sup>[63](/bible/1-kings/8#v63)</sup> And Solomon offered a sacrifice of peace offerings, which he offered unto the Lord, two and twenty thousand oxen, and an hundred and twenty thousand sheep. So the king and all the children of Israel dedicated the house of the Lord.
>
> <sup>[64](/bible/1-kings/8#v64)</sup> The same day did the king hallow the middle of the court that was before the house of the Lord: for there he offered burnt offerings, and meat offerings, and the fat of the peace offerings: because the brasen altar that was before the Lord was too little to receive the burnt offerings, and meat offerings, and the fat of the peace offerings.
>
> <sup>[65](/bible/1-kings/8#v65)</sup> And at that time Solomon held a feast, and all Israel with him, a great congregation, from the entering in of Hamath unto the river of Egypt, before the Lord our God, seven days and seven days, even fourteen days.
>
> <sup>[66](/bible/1-kings/8#v66)</sup> On the eighth day he sent the people away: and they blessed the king, and went unto their tents joyful and glad of heart for all the goodness that the Lord had done for David his servant, and for Israel his people.

- The king and all Israel offer sacrifices before the Lord, Solomon offering a peace offering of twenty-two thousand oxen and a hundred and twenty thousand sheep, so the king and all the people dedicate the house of the Lord. He hallows the middle of the court to offer there because the brazen altar was too little to receive the multitude of offerings.
- Solomon holds a feast, and all Israel with him from the entering in of Hamath to the river of Egypt, before the Lord seven days and seven days, even fourteen days. On the eighth day he sends the people away, and they bless the king and go to their tents joyful and glad of heart for all the goodness the Lord had done for David and for Israel his people.
